title: Promotional digital content is advertising
description: Any communication promoting an RMP's or hospital's services, reputation, skills, qualifications, achievements or facilities is an advertisement, including social-media, sponsored, targeted, influencer-led, search-engine, platform-based, audio-visual and AI-generated or AI-assisted content with a promotional character. Non-promotional public information without commercial intent is exempt.

title: Equipment/facility information must be purely factual
description: Availability or installation of equipment, technology, diagnostic facilities or services may be shared only as factual information, without claims of superiority, guaranteed accuracy, guaranteed outcomes, comparative claims or other unverifiable representations.

title: RMP electronic posts must disclose identity and registration
description: An RMP publishing any electronic media post must transparently disclose name, qualifications, registration status and SMR/NMR registration number.

title: Clinical establishment posts must disclose RMP details
description: Clinical establishments publishing electronic media posts must disclose the names of RMPs with qualifications, registration status and SMR/NMR registration number.

title: No fake, paid or solicited reviews and testimonials
description: No RMP or hospital shall solicit, purchase, procure, manipulate or publish fake, paid or misleading reviews, ratings, testimonials, endorsements or recommendations. An RMP shall not request or share patient testimonials, recommendations, endorsements or reviews for professional promotion on social media.

title: Third-party publication does not absolve responsibility
description: Publishing through a digital platform, third party, advertising agency, influencer or intermediary does not absolve the RMP or institution of responsibility for content it authorized, commissioned, sponsored, adopted or knowingly permitted.

title: Health education must not promote personal practice
description: Health awareness programmes, campaigns, academic discussions and educational content are allowed only if they do not promote personal practice, do not solicit patients and are not monetized through promotional marketing.

title: Hoardings/billboards limited to factual information
description: Public hoardings and billboards (municipal, transport, railways, airports etc.) may be used only for factual information such as infrastructure and facilities. Unverified or unverifiable claims are treated as commercial and prohibited.

title: Patient information not to be used in advertising
description: Patient information, photographs, videos, records, clinical images, treatment details, testimonials or identifiable information shall not be used for advertising unless permitted by law with valid consent. Consent does not make an otherwise prohibited testimonial, endorsement, patient story, before-and-after depiction or success claim permissible.

title: Patient identity must be protected
description: Patient data such as names, faces, birth marks, identification marks or anomalies that can identify a patient must not be shared publicly; even lawful disclosures must crop, blur or black out identifying details.

title: AI-generated commercial promotional campaigns prohibited; AI content must be labelled
description: AI-generated promotional campaigns for commercial interest are prohibited. Any permissible AI-generated promotional content must carry a source mark explicitly stating the content is AI-generated.

title: No misleading AI content about treatment or outcomes
description: AI-generated or AI-assisted content must not create misleading, deceptive or unverifiable representations about diagnosis, treatment, clinical outcomes, qualifications, patient experiences or healthcare services.

title: No synthetic patients, doctors or endorsements
description: AI must not create or manipulate a patient's image, testimonial, voice or clinical outcome, or create synthetic endorsements purporting to be from an actual patient, RMP or other person. Materially AI-altered content must be disclosed.

title: No commercial broadcast of surgical procedures
description: Live broadcast or commercial dissemination of surgical or clinical procedures is not permitted except as allowed under NMC live-surgery guidelines on safety, consent, privacy, educational purpose and sponsorship.

title: Advertising using personal data must follow IT Act and DPDP Act
description: Processing, publication or disclosure of digital personal data in advertising must comply with the IT Act 2000 and the Digital Personal Data Protection Act 2023 and Rules 2025.

title: No fear-based marketing or demand creation
description: RMPs shall not advertise to create unnecessary demand for procedures, promote unnecessary diagnostics or use fear-based marketing.

title: No patient solicitation or self-promotion
description: RMPs shall not solicit patients directly or indirectly, self-promote professional services, engage third parties to market medical services, permit use of their name, image, voice, testimonial or endorsement to promote services or products, or join campaigns that commercialize medical practice.

title: No success rates, patient counts or exaggerated claims
description: RMPs shall not advertise personal achievements, success rates or number of patients treated, or use claims such as 'Guaranteed cure', 'Best doctor', 'No.1 Specialist', '100% success', 'painless treatment', 'Miracle treatment', 'Exclusive cure' or any other unverifiable or exaggerated claim.

title: No doctor endorsement of drugs or products
description: An RMP shall not give any approval, recommendation, endorsement, certificate or statement for any drug, medicine, remedy, device, diagnostic, health or commercial product for advertising using their name, signature, photograph, voice or professional status, paid or unpaid.

title: No before-and-after photos, surgical results or celebrity patients
description: RMPs shall not publish cases for promotion, advertise surgical results, display before-and-after photographs, publicize celebrity patients or promote success stories, unless strictly for scientific or educational purposes with anonymized patient consent.

title: No unrealistic expectations, hidden risks or unproven therapies
description: No statement that creates unrealistic expectations, misrepresents outcomes, conceals risks, or promotes unproven therapies or secret remedies whose composition, scientific basis, safety or efficacy is not established.

title: No commissions, referral or lead-generation fees
description: No commission, rebate, bonus, gift, referral fee, lead-generation fee or consideration linked to referral or procurement of patients, specimens or materials. Agency, influencer or platform arrangements must not tie payment to patient referral.

title: No unverifiable superiority or ranking claims
description: No claims such as 'best', 'No.1', 'leading', 'most trusted', 'top', 'number one', 'unmatched' unless objectively verifiable through a transparent, independent methodology. Rankings or awards cited must be independently verifiable with methodology, date and awarding body disclosed.

title: No discounts, offers, coupons or free procedures as inducement
description: No discounts, limited-period offers, contests, coupons, gifts, cashbacks, referral benefits or free procedures likely to encourage unnecessary consultation, investigation or treatment. Disclosure of fees or packages must be factual and transparent.

title: No celebrity, influencer or patient endorsements
description: No celebrity, influencer, patient, employee or third party may promote professional services through testimonials, endorsements or recommendations. Material commercial relationships must be disclosed; intermediaries cannot do indirectly what is prohibited directly.

title: No fake engagement or ranking manipulation
description: No procuring or manipulating fake followers, likes, reviews, ratings, testimonials, comments or views, or manipulating search rankings or algorithms to create a misleading impression of professional standing.

title: Permitted RMP communications
description: Permitted: research case studies published in reputed journals; factual, non-promotional announcements of starting practice, change of practice type or address, temporary absence, resumption or succession of practice, and public declaration of charges; public-health talks without promoting the employer; patient education leaflets without cure guarantees or superiority claims; greetings on national or medical days without professional promotion.

title: Hospital advertising limited to factual, verifiable information
description: Hospitals may share factual, objective, verifiable information on name, location, contact, departments, facilities, equipment, services, emergency services, accreditation and charges. It must not contain solicitation, inducements, comparative superiority claims, guarantees of cure or outcome, exaggerated claims or promotional portrayal of an individual RMP. A doctor directory serving patient information is not treated as an advertisement.

title: No promotional use of a doctor's photograph
description: Use of an RMP's photograph or image for self-advertisement, solicitation or promotional publicity is not permitted, including on letterheads or signboards, per IMC Regulations 6.1.1 and 6.1.2.

title: Healthcare platforms: no paid doctor rankings
description: Healthcare platforms hosting RMPs must follow NMC ethical advertising norms, must not offer paid ranking of doctors and must keep listing practices transparent.

title: Penalty framework for violations
description: Graded action by State Medical Council: first violation - warning and ethics training; second - censure and monetary penalty; third - suspension 3-6 months; serious violations (misleading cure claims, patient inducement, digital mass solicitation) - suspension 6-12 months; repeated violations - removal from register for 1-3 years. Hospitals are dealt with under the Clinical Establishments Act.
